newsitem.title: USA: Spectranetics cleared to end part of trial.
newsitem.headline: Spectranetics cleared to end part of trial.

text.p: Spectranetics Corp said on Wednesday it had received clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to end random clinical trials of the company's excimer laser.
The laser removes pacemaker leads imbedded in the human heart.
The FDA action allows physicians involved in the trial to now recommend laser removal over other extraction methods rather than putting patients through a random selection process, the company said.
The FDA also approved expansion of the trial from 14 clinical sites to 20 and increased the number of patients who can be treated with the laser to 600 from 282.
Pacing leads are the conduit through which pacemakers regulate the heartbeat with electrical pulses, the company said.
Old leads that have become ineffective have been left in place because they are often heavily embedded in scar tissue, making extraction traumatic and potentially dangerous, the company said.
